newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-EMU drives bond markets to diverge in 97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-EMU drives bond markets to diverge in 97.

text.p: The launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) will produce mixed bond market performances in 1997 and beyond, recent Reuters surveys show.

Looking at the spread of 10-year bonds against the 10-year German Bund, Spain and Portugal's government bonds are expected to show continued but slower convergence. Italian BTPs, which performed spectacularly well in 1996, will lag Bunds, while French OATs will see little change.
In Britain, gilts will have to wait until after a general election to enjoy better times but then the outlook improves.
The spreads reflect the premium at which a country's bonds trade over another market, typically benchmark German Bunds.

Spanish and Portuguese bonds are expected to shave their yield spreads versus the core German market to an average of around 60 basis points by the end of 1997, a survey of 11 analysts showed. At 1030 GMT on Wednesday the spreads stood at 88 and 78 respectively.

Iberian spreads have seen a massive tightening on expectations that Spain and Portugal will help launch the single European currency in 1999. If the two want to participate in a single currency, their spreads should narrow close to zero by 1999.
Reuters most recent EMU survey showed only 30 percent and 27 percent of the panellists expected Spain and Portugal respectively to join EMU on its target January 1, 1999 start date.
Thus the market may have to re-evaluate its optimistic stance on the two countries, some analysts said.

"Even given a 100 percent probability of Spain and Portugal entering EMU from its start, a spread at any level from 75 basis points to 100 basis points is normal because of exchange rate risk," said a Banco Cisf analyst.

But Italian government bonds are expected to underperform over the year. Economists in Reuters latest quarterly economic survey for Italy predicted the 10-year BTP/Bund spread would widen slightly to around 165 basis points by the end of March, returning to 155 by the year end. It was around 142 basis points earlier on Wednesday.

In France, widely expected to join a single currency at its inception, the forecast is for OATs to narrow against their German equivalent. The OAT/Bund spread was expected to converge from its current minus 14 to parity by the end of 1997.

British government bonds could suffer until after a general election, with the gilt/Bund spread expected to hit 200 basis points at the end of March, according to an average of forecasts in Reuters January survey on the British economy.

The election is due by May 22, and once political uncertainty is removed, gilts should outperform. The poll showed the spread narrowing to around 160 basis points from a current 182 by the end of the year.

"The presence of electoral uncertainty will hinder gilts over the middle of this year," said Philip Shaw, group economist at Union Plc. But once the market gets to grips with a new government, gilts should rally. The gilt/Bund spread was expected to fall still further to 128 basis points by the end of 1998.

"Markets dont really think that (British) EMU entry in 1999 is an option. But there are some residual hopes that the UK could participate by 2002 and that could be one of the factors driving the spread down in two years' time," Shaw said.
But if EMU's launch stalls, then bond markets could well suffer. Germany would appear a relative safe haven, and spreads could remain wide for a longer period of time.
"Markets would fear that budgetary discipline had broken down. All European bonds would suffer, but the peripheral markets would suffer the most vis--vis Bunds," added Shaw.
